title: Over-protection

D0.outcome: Explains over-protecting a strategically important point as giving it more defence than the attack seems to need, so that the defenders become active by contact with it.

D1.outcome: In a given position, names the point that deserves over-protection and the pieces that will do it.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides whether a point should be over-protected or whether that would make the defenders passive.

D3.outcome: Predicts how the absence of pressure on the point turns over-protection into passive defence.

misconceptions: Over-protection is the same as passive defence.
conditions: The point is strong and will come under pressure; the pieces involved do not become passive.
Practical, not proven; the examples are won games by a strong player (survivor bias).
contrasts: Over-protecting an ordinary weak point makes the defenders passive.
Over-protecting the base of a chain that needs no extra defence.
The point is under no pressure.
note: Heavily conditioned; label practical not proven (Nimz sheet §10 Q5).
